title: Contractor-to-Perm Hire Calibration Cookbook (WIP)
content:
Purpose: Capture a lightweight, repeatable process and scorecard for evaluating contractors for conversion to full-time roles. This is a working cookbook to help hiring managers, people ops partners, and Eng leads align on signals, thresholds, and onboarding commitments for contractor->perm conversions.

Scope and use-cases:
- Short-term contractors (3-9 months) with product/infra impact being considered for a headcount conversion.
- Applies when the org expects to convert without an external open role (backfill/promotion-style) and also as a reusable rubric for conversion interviews.
- Not meant to replace standard hiring panel for external senior IC/hiring; instead, a calibration layer and checklist to speed decisions.

Quick decisions we want to enable:
1) Convert now (fast-track) -> offer and 30-day ramp plan.
2) Convert with evidence (extend contractor, focused project + eval).
3) Do not convert now -> close feedback and candidate uplift plan or offboarding.

When to run a calibration:
- Contractor has delivered >= 2 cross-functional features or owned a critical bug fix/incident during their contract window.
- Hiring manager requests conversion OR People Ops raises a capacity-driven conversion candidate.
- At 6-8 months into a long contractor assignment as a routine check.

Owners and cadence:
- Hiring manager (owner): prepares conversion packet and initial recommendation.
- People Ops partner: facilitates panel scheduling, ensures rubric completion, owns offer templates and equity/comp calibration.
- Eng lead/Tech Manager: provides technical calibration and bias review.
- Timeline target: decision within 10 business days from panel.

Conversion packet checklist (what hiring manager submits before panel):
- Short summary (1 paragraph) of contributions and why conversion is being considered.
- 2–3 measurable outcomes with dates (PRs shipped, incidents led, latency/throughput improvements, customer feedback).
- Code samples or design docs (links).
- Feedback snapshot: 1–3 lines from cross-functional partners (PM, SRE, Product Design).
- Current contractor compensation & proposed FT comp band (prelim).

Calibration rubric (5 signal categories, 1–4 scale; guidance below):
- Impact (deliverables completed, product outcomes, customer impact).
- Ownership & reliability (independent shipping, incident leadership, follow-through).
- Technical competency & craft (code quality, design rigor, system thinking).
- Collaboration & communication (async docs, cross-team work, mentorship).
- Growth mindset & role fit (coachability, curiosity, product sense).

Scoring guidance (scale explanation):
- 4 = Exceeds expectations for target level (clear promotable signal).
- 3 = Fully meets expectations and reliable in role.
- 2 = Meets some expectations; needs focused work in 1 area.
- 1 = Does not meet expectations; recommend another path.

Calibration thresholds (recommended):
- Fast-track convert: average >= 3.5 and no individual category < 3.
- Convert with evidence plan: average between 3.0–3.49 OR any one category == 2 but rest >=3.
- Do not convert: average < 3.0 or more than one category == 2.

Interview/panel composition for calibration session (30–60m):
- Hiring manager (chair) – 10–15m summary and Q&A.
- Peer engineer (level-equal) – technical questions and code sample review.
- Engineering manager or tech lead – system design and ownership discussion.
- Product partner or PM (optional) – product sense and impact.
- People Ops partner – comp calibration and role definition.

Panel agenda template (45m):
- 0–5m: Introductions & purpose.
- 5–15m: Hiring manager packet highlights and contribution review.
- 15–30m: Technical deep-dive (PRs/design, ask clarifying questions).
- 30–40m: Behavioral & collaboration probes.
- 40–45m: Panel scoring + next steps (People Ops captures decision).

Sample behavioral probes (tailored for contractors):
- Tell us about a time during this contract you had to pivot work due to changing priorities. How did you communicate that?
- Describe a live incident you helped resolve. What was your direct contribution and what did you learn?
- When you handed off your work, what did you do to ensure continuity?

Technical probes (3 focused areas):
- Walk through a recent PR that changed production behavior: why the approach, risk tradeoffs, test strategy, and follow-up monitoring.
- Describe a performance debugging story: hypothesis, measurement, and root-cause.
- Design question: how would you design a light-weight KV caching layer for low-latency reads (focus on constraints we have at Redwood: cost, mem, eviction)?

Scorecard template (copy into panel notes):
- Candidate name: 
- Role / target level: 
- Scores: Impact / Ownership / Tech / Collaboration / Growth -> numeric (1–4) each
- Avg score: 
- Panel recommendation (fast-track / evidence-plan / no-convert): 
- Recommended ramp or evidence plan (if applicable): 30/60/90 day milestones

Offer & comp notes (People Ops checklist):
- Confirm headcount and band availability before offer. If not available, discuss 3 options: create headcount, extend contractor (with evidence plan), or re-open req.
- Fast-track offers: target T+3 business days for verbal once approved.
- Include a 30/60/90 performance checkpoint in offer doc for clarity.
- Equity guidance: follow same leveling calibration as external hires; document rationale for deviations.

Onboarding & ramp plan (30/60/90 with minimal friction):
- Day 0–7: access audit (git, infra, slack, okta), 1:1 with manager, team async playbook share, identify buddy.
- Week 2–4: small ownership area transition, paired work on critical path, join product rituals.
- Month 2: independently own a medium-scope ticket and write a post-mortem or design note.
- Month 3: deliver measurable outcome and present learnings to team.

Fast access checklist (practical) – tick before start:
- OKTA invite & MFA set up.
- GitHub org membership and repo write access.
- Cloud console access (least privilege) + SRE ticket for role.
- Pager on-call training (if role requires).
- Slack channels + engineering wiki permissions.

Communication templates (short):
- Manager -> Candidate verbal: "We would like to convert you to full time. This is a verbal offer pending comp and sign-off; we’ll share written offer by [date]."
- Manager -> Team announcement: short blurb with start date, role, and immediate projects.

Open questions and unresolved items (please comment):
- How strict should People Ops be with the headcount-first rule for conversions when a contractor is high-performing but headcount is limited? (current bias: document the business case; consider short-term reserve band).
- Do we standardize a 10% premium for contractor conversion as recognition of ramp risk? (mixed feedback in sync with Finance).
- Should evidence-plan extensions be capped at one 3-month extension or more flexible?

Action items (owners):
- Aisha: finalize rubric language and share with Eng leads for feedback by 2026-02-20.
- Marcus: mock-run this rubric on 3 recent conversions and capture delta vs historical decisions.
- Lina: draft People Ops offer template language for 30/60/90 checkpoints.

Notes to self / quick hacks:
- Use Slack thread template: /add-thread "Contractor Convert: <name>" with tag @people-ops for asynchronous comments.
- When possible attach PR links in packet to save panel time.
- Keep calibration panels <= 45m to avoid over-committee and speed decisions.

Appendix: quick checklist for hiring managers preparing packet (copyable):
1) 1-paragraph summary of why conversion.
2) 2 measurable outcomes + links.
3) Short cross-functional referee comments (PM, SRE).
4) Proposed band & justification.
5) 30/60/90 draft goals.

End of doc (WIP). Please add examples of past packets or anonymized scorecards below — we will iterate and lock policy Q2 2026.
